subject.title: Telegram voice message delayed ~15 minutes before agent dispatch, then run aborts

question: What Telegram behavior should OpenClaw use when a source message is much older than dispatch time or a direct voice-message turn aborts before any visible reply?
rationale: The code gap is real, but thresholds, restart/alert policy, retry behavior, and direct-message fallback copy are product and reliability choices that automation should not pick without maintainer intent.

options.title: Define Narrow Watchdog And Fallback
options.body: Specify a source-age threshold, diagnostic/restart behavior, and direct-message failure fallback, then require focused tests plus live Telegram proof before implementation.

options.title: Route Only Polling Sleep Gap First
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/86541 as the first narrow liveness fix while keeping this issue open for the remaining voice abort/no-reply behavior.

options.title: Wait For Live Reproduction
options.body: Keep the issue blocked on a current-main live Telegram repro before choosing any watchdog or user-facing fallback semantics.

recommendation.title: Define Narrow Watchdog And Fallback
recommendation.body: Specify a source-age threshold, diagnostic/restart behavior, and direct-message failure fallback, then require focused tests plus live Telegram proof before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest sampled history across the current Telegram liveness module and broader Telegram dispatch surface, making him the best available owner for the behavior choice.
